description: Supplemental single-violation negative variants for blind decision. Each gives a base, a mutation, the repairs and isolation recipes, the target role and the one rule it violates; expected outcomes are withheld. Parents are the neg-NN cases you already decided; this file does not name them.

conventions.ISO-BOTH: Apply the parent's mutation identically to BOTH header/index copies of the sidecar (primary at block 0, tail at block H+P). Recompute each copy's canonical_metadata_hash; the two hashes are equal, because copy_kind is excluded from the hash. Then recompute each copy's header_crc64 (0xC0) and block0_crc64 (B-8). Write that hash into the footer (0x60) and recompute footer_crc64 (0x80). Write it into the ParityMap directory entry for the sidecar (key 8) and apply R-PM-PAYLOAD from negative-cases.json. Any field the footer or directory entry mirrors (H 0x38/key 6, P 0x40/key 7, total 0x48/key 5, range 0x28/0x30/keys 3-4) gets the new value there too, when that mirror has no rule of its own the value would break. A mutation confined to hash-excluded bytes (copy_kind, the reserved fields, copy_generation) changes neither the footer nor the directory. Result: the Section 9.1 primary/tail agreement, the footer comparison of Section 13.3 step 1 and the directory hash check all hold.
conventions.ISO-FAULT-FOOTER: Used when the footer mirrors the field under its own rule (primary start = 0, tail start = H + P) or with a rule the text leaves unstated (the footer's tape_uuid). The harness presents the sidecar's footer block (block 2H+P) as unreadable: it returns a medium error for that one block read and changes no byte. With no footer, the footer comparison takes no part. The Recoverer proceeds by Section 13.3 steps 2 and 3, and a Scanner in a BOT walk uses item 5. A medium error is damage, not a format violation (Section 15: 'I/O faults MUST remain distinct from format violations').
conventions.ISO-REBUILD: Used when the new value changes the sidecar's physical length. Rebuild the image with the sidecar at its new block count, then regenerate everything that depends on the prefix: the replicas' structural row for the sidecar; the ParityMap directory entry (keys 5-8); the ParityMap's canonical_map_digest (header/footer 0x58 and payload key 5), payload_sha256 and CRCs; all three replicas (payload, canonical-map, edition, layout and descriptor digests; the five component tuples; the local planned tape-file and start fields; EOD; footer observations; header-record hashes; CRCs); and both separation extents (tuples, predecessor/successor fields, descriptor digests, header-record hashes, CRCs). Every terminal LBA shifts by the change in the sidecar's block count.
conventions.UNIT: The rule can be reached only at unit level: the named computation of the named role, called with the listed inputs. The reason field says why no byte image can present these inputs while every other rule of the role holds.
conventions.erratum_to_frozen_concurrent_checks: Several frozen 7a cases mutate one copy only: sidecar-copy-generation, sidecar-copy-kind-reserved, sidecar-header-reserved variants a and b, sidecar-data-crc-count, sidecar-footer-index, sidecar-header-block-count, sidecar-inline-index-bytes, sidecar-logical-shard-count, sidecar-parity-block-count, sidecar-primary-start, sidecar-real-data-shard-count, sidecar-tail-start, sidecar-tape-uuid, sidecar-total-block-count a/b, sidecar-k-zero, sidecar-m-zero and sidecar-s-zero. Each of these also breaks the Section 9.1 primary/tail agreement rule ('only copy_kind and the recomputed CRCs differ'), and several frozen concurrent_checks lists do not say so. The three cases whose lists name no other rule at all (sidecar-copy-generation, sidecar-copy-kind-reserved, sidecar-header-reserved variant a) are included below.

mutation.input: the commit record for tape file 2 (the sidecar) claims block_count 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF; object records and ranges are unchanged

integrity_repair: none on tape; the injected record must be well formed in the implementation's commit-record format
variants.target: the Resumer's Σ(block_count + 1) over the prefix (Section 3.2, used at Section 14 step 4 and by any LBA-based positioning in step 3)
variants.every_other_rule_holds: The huge count sits on a sidecar, so T = 6 and W = 4 are unaffected, unlike the parent, whose huge Object count also overflowed T. Step 2 holds: T − W = 2 < S*k = 4, W ≤ T, the ranges are contiguous from 0 to W, the epoch ids are consecutive, and the final object ends at T. A single record makes no conflicting claim (Section 3.4). The re-read of [4,6) in step 3 finds data where it is expected, when positioning is by filemarks.

integrity_repair: ISO-BOTH (hash-excluded: CRCs of both copies only)
variants.every_other_rule_holds: Both copies carry the same value, so they agree. The hash excludes reserved fields, so the footer and directory still match. Nothing else changes.

variants.target: primary/tail agreement (Section 9.1), as run by a Verifier or a BOT-walk Scanner that parses both copies
variants.violates_only: Section 9.1 'When both copies parse, a Reader MUST verify that they agree and reject divergence'
variants.every_other_rule_holds: Each copy on its own satisfies Sections 9.2-9.5, with a hash equal to the SHA-256 of its own bytes. The footer is unreadable, so neither copy is compared with a footer hash. The directory's key 8 matches the primary. A directory comparison happens only in the step-3 rescue, which the valid primary makes unnecessary, and no rule compares the directory with a parsed copy otherwise.

base.artifact: tape-image a4-minimal, rebuilt: the sidecar at tape file 2 becomes 8 blocks

mutation.field: sidecar_total_block_count (0x70) = 8 in both copies; footer total (0x48) = 8; directory key 5 = 8; replica structural row block_count = 8
mutation.file_layout: blocks 0 primary, 1..4 parity, 5 tail, 6 footer (at footer_block_index = 2H + P = 6), 7 an all-zero block

variants.every_other_rule_holds: The header total equals the measured count, 8 (Scanner item 5, Section 16.2). The tail start 5 = H + P and footer index 6 = 2H + P hold, and the footer is at block 6. The footer's fields agree with both copies, including total 8, which equals the measured count. The copies agree. The directory entry and the map agree on block count 8. Block 7 is the extra block that the declared total implies. It breaks no rule of its own: it does not parse as a footer, and Section 13.3 treats an unparseable last block as a fallback, not a violation.

base.role: replica footer arithmetic (Section 10.4), applied to separation footers too by Section 10.6

variants.target: backward start delta = observed record count − 1
variants.every_other_rule_holds: Image level is impossible: the footer's observations MUST equal the plan (Section 8.3), and every planned component has at least two records (Section 8.3). An observed count of 0 therefore always also breaks the plan-equality rule.

variants.violates_only: Checked evaluation of 2^46 × 2^18 (the exact total_records = 2^46 fits)
variants.every_other_rule_holds: total ≥ 2, footer_offset and interior fit. Image level is impossible: the recorded total record count must equal ceil(E/B) = 2^46, and the extent's measured record count must equal it, which needs 2^64 bytes of medium.
